title: Gravediggers bury
html_source:
Hamlet Act V, Scene 1 begins with two “clowns” digging a grave for Ophelia. Horatio and Hamlet (the prince/pere) arrive. One clown debates with Hamlet about whose grave it is, as follows:

HAMLET: Who is to be buried in’t?
First Clown: One that was a woman, sir; but, rest her soul, she’s dead.

The scene, like this section of Stephen’s discourse, examines the nature of being, and the nature of the personhood of the deceased.
